A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, renamed from GANTASTIC to ViDiT, with matching authors, core objectives, editing equations, and retained results. All pages, including both appendices, support comparison through text extraction and visual inspection.

before.justification: v1 reports original editing experiments, qualitative ablations, LPIPS comparisons, CLIP rescoring, and a 50-participant user study, with additional experimental results in its appendix.

after.justification: v2 reports original quantitative comparisons and ablations, editing examples from multiple supervision sources, a 40-participant user study, and appendix experiments including failure cases.

M1.justification: The supervision interface is generalized: v1 Algorithm 1 constructs pairs from StyleGAN latent codes and a style-space direction, whereas v2 accepts image-edit pairs from any editing source, demonstrated with StyleGAN-NADA and Prompt2Prompt. The learned conditional embedding, semantic and latent losses, additive guidance, multidirectional composition, and DDPM inversion remain substantively unchanged.

E1.justification: v2 adds artistic transformations such as Ukiyoe and Pixar through StyleGAN-NADA supervision, and evaluates attribute transfer to illustrations and paintings (Fig. 3 and appendix Figs. 15–16). These extend the represented domains and editing tasks beyond v1's photographic/generated face and animal examples. FFHQ and AFHQ coverage is retained; real-image editing already appeared in v1.

E2.justification: v2 adds evaluated InstructPix2Pix, Prompt2Prompt, Weights2Weights, IP-Adapter, Attribute-Control, PnP-Diffusion, MasaCtrl, Asyrp, and DiffAE comparisons, and includes W+ Adapter quantitatively. It removes v1's Cycle Diffusion, Diffusion Pullback/NoiseCLR, and StyleCLIP/LatentCLR/SeFa/GANSpace comparisons. SEGA, Concept Sliders, LEDITS++, and qualitative W+ Adapter comparisons were already present, including in v1's appendix.

E3.justification: Default training sample count changes from 100 to 1000. v2 explicitly defaults to full-timestep editing, whereas v1 recommends 0.4T. Evaluation expands beyond LPIPS and CLIP rescoring to DINO, DreamSim, and CLIP/SigLIP similarity metrics, with a new 100-generated-sample comparison and a 200-pair Asian/Smile comparison. The reported user-study participant count changes from 50 to 40; these disclosures do not establish that retained results were rerun.

E4.justification: v2 retains the qualitative timestep, sample-size, and loss ablations while adding quantitative sample-size/loss results in Table 1. It introduces a DDIM-versus-DDPM inversion ablation in Fig. 6(b), expands composition demonstrations, and adds explicit subtle-edit failure cases in Appendix C/Fig. 11. These add substantial diagnostic evidence beyond the earlier qualitative analyses.

E5.justification: v1 explicitly states that all experiments use random seed 0; v2 omits that information. Neither version reports repeated-run variability, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The omission establishes a reporting change, not an actual change of seeds or run counts.

E6.justification: v2 adds quantitative results in Tables 1–3 and new source-transfer, stylized-image, inversion, and failure examples. v1's attribute-specific LPIPS comparison is replaced by a differently scoped comparison reporting ViDiT LPIPS 0.030, so a same-setting gain cannot be inferred. User-study results add InstructPix2Pix 2.06 and Prompt2Prompt 2.74 while removing Cycle Diffusion 2.65. The retained methods' study means and the entire rescoring matrix are unchanged.

T1.justification: Algorithm 1 corrects the edited-image noising expression from x_i plus noise in v1 to x'_i plus noise in v2, bringing the pseudocode into agreement with the intended paired-image objective. The principal loss and guidance equations remain equivalent, and neither version supplies theorems or proofs. The expanded mechanism discussion is explanatory rather than new theory.

C1.justification: v1 centers its contribution on transferring GAN directions to diffusion models without finetuning and achieving competitive GAN/diffusion editing. v2 claims a universal, source-agnostic visual-direction framework that overcomes textual description limits and provides superior identity preservation across styles. Reusable zero-shot directions already existed in v1; the substantive expansion concerns source generality, applicability, and comparative positioning.

C2.justification: v2 adds explanations contrasting globally pooled CLIP features with spatial denoising predictions, interprets cross-domain transfer as evidence against overfitting, and identifies limitations of global directions and subtle supervision changes. It reverses the timestep interpretation despite retaining the displayed examples. Its new ethics discussion also asserts that observed biases originate entirely in pretrained components.

D1.justification: v2 omits v1's Stable Diffusion v1.5 identifier, learning rate 5e-3, batch size 8, and approximately 30-minute direction-training time, while retaining AdamW, 1000 iterations, L40 hardware, and approximately five-second editing. It adds the NTI+Prompt2Prompt implementation choice, a 60-pair user-study disclosure and example question, and a changed project address. These are documentation changes, not established changes to omitted settings.

R1.justification: Related work is substantially reoriented from GAN latent-space discovery toward visual versus textual conditioning and source-independent transfer. v2 adds substantive discussions of newer conditioning and editing approaches, including IP-Adapter, Weights2Weights, Attribute-Control, InstructPix2Pix, and DiffAE, while removing the dedicated GAN exploration survey and numerous associated citations. The novelty positioning changes beyond bibliographic updates.

P1.justification: The title and method name change, and the abstract, introduction, related work, and method narrative are extensively rewritten around 'Learn Once, Edit Anywhere.' StyleGAN preliminaries are removed, the training algorithm moves from the appendix into the method section, limitations and ethics become separate sections, and the appendix is reorganized.

P2.justification: The document changes from two-column to single-column layout, redraws the overview and framework figures, reorganizes horizontal ablation panels vertically, and adds several quantitative tables and qualitative displays. Earlier GAN/diffusion-direction comparison figures disappear. Several appendix displays are retained and relocated, including v1 Figs. S.11–S.13 becoming v2 Figs. 7–9, rather than constituting new results.

improvement.justification: New supervision sources, multi-metric comparisons, inversion analysis, and explicit failures strengthen the evaluation. However, v2 removes important reproducibility details and reverses the timestep conclusion for retained examples. Its claim of consistently improving LPIPS/DINO with sample size also contradicts Table 1: from N=10 to 100, LPIPS worsens from 0.098 to 0.136 and DINO falls from 0.869 to 0.842. These material reporting problems coexist with substantive benefits, preventing a reliable net quality judgment.
